07 · ICE in practice · Work with the team

Score the work together, then agree the priority

Start with the task list. Discuss each score with BD and engineering.

I

Impact

How much value could it create?

1–10
  • How much time could it save weekly?
  • Does the benefit grow with usage?
  • Does it remove a bottleneck?
  • What changes for capacity or revenue?

High score = meaningful business value

C

Confidence

How strong is the evidence?

1–10
  • Is the process clearly defined?
  • Do we understand the exceptions?
  • Are tools, access and integrations verified?
  • Has a similar approach worked before?

High score = stronger supporting evidence

E

Ease

How feasible is the implementation?

1–10
  • How many systems are involved?
  • How complex are the rules and logic?
  • How long will it take to build?
  • What dependencies or approvals exist?

High score = easier to implement

A shared decision

Discuss the scores.
Build ownership and trust.

BDExplains effort, value and real-world exceptions.

EngineeringChallenges feasibility, access and dependencies.

TogetherAgree the priority and what the pilot must prove.

ICE = (Impact + Confidence + Ease) ÷ 3Our equal-weight method · Higher is better

A score guides the experiment.
Measured results justify the rollout.

Based on the supplied ICE framework. Fictional scores and workshop assumptions; real team alignment and pilot evidence remain to be collected.

10 · Engineering judgment · Choosing the approach

When does a workflow need AI?

Choose the approach based on how much interpretation the task needs.

Clear rules

CODE

Validate dates
Calculate KPIs
Convert minutes to hours

Varied inputs

CODE + AI

Map spreadsheet headers
Extract facts from notes
Check values with code

Ambiguous meaning

AI + CHECKS

Surface conflicting updates
Interpret meeting context
Summarize complex discussions

Use code for clear rules. Use AI for interpretation.
Test a stronger model only when simpler approaches fall short.

Greater ambiguity → more evaluation and safeguards. Model size follows measured quality needs.

15 · Model choice · Measured evidence

Haiku for AI-assisted drafting

Provisional choice: preserve important BD context at a low token cost.

Why this choice?

Only $0.23 more / 1,000

Than Mistral, while keeping the open BD action and passing all quote checks.

Gemini: fastest, but omitted that action.
Mistral: cheapest; one quote changed a line break.

Haiku’s weakness: incorrect owner wording and inconsistent review flags. A person still checks every report.

What changes as the workflow grows?

More reports → scale the service

Add queues, shared storage and rate controls. Volume alone does not justify a heavier model.

Harder documents → test a stronger model

Beyond the 40k-character intake cap, fix extraction and split inputs first. Persistent critical fact loss → compare a stronger model on unseen cases.

Provider constraints → reassess the provider

If retention, region or throughput needs are unmet, qualify an alternative. Recheck permissions and quality before switching.

6 synthetic cases × 2 runs per model; assistant review, human sign-off pending. Costs extrapolate the tested input mix and exclude review, retries and infrastructure. Scaling triggers are proposed; retention was not tested. Full evidence ↗

Claude Haiku 5.5Gemini 3.5 Flash-LiteMistral Small 2603

Appendix 1 · Supporting detail

My starting assumptions

The assumptions I have used to explore the workflow and estimate its potential value.

Three working assumptions and how to validate them
What I am assumingHow I would validate it
The report follows a stable weekly structure. CSV exports, notes, and engineering updates are available to its owner.Inspect representative source packs, confirm access, and document missing inputs and exceptions.
Each of 10 BD managers spends 8h/week on report production + review, falling to 2h; surrounding manual work does not increase.Time the full process, including collection, spreadsheet repair and review. Subtract extra work and avoid double-counting shared reports.
BD will adopt the report and use the released time for partner conversations and onboarding preparation.Run a BD pilot. Track use of the report, review effort, and how the team reallocates its time.

Hypothesis: 10 managers × 6 hours = 60 hours/week, or 2,760 hours over 46 reporting weeks. Track whether that capacity supports qualified opportunities and partner launches. Fewer users or smaller net savings reduce the capacity released.

Appendix 3 · Assisted intake · Benchmark complete, feature not built

Gemini 3.8 Flash for unstructured data

Proposed between steps 2 & 3 when files are uploaded

Best complete results in this suite

117 / 120 passed, including all 30 holdout calls. No wrong values in completed responses.

A small cost premium

+$1.07 per 1,000 intakes versus Haiku. Mistral is cheaper, but supplied 18 substantively wrong values.

Weaknesses to address

3 timeouts; 3s median, 22s p95 latency.
Test retries. Published Gemini rates double in January 2027.

Confidentiality is a gate

No account is cleared for confidential files. Classify before sending; verify enterprise terms, retention and permitted regions. store=false ≠ zero retention.

40 synthetic cases × 3 runs/model; independent human review pending. Costs: USD tokens for this input mix, excluding retries and infrastructure. Full evidence & provider policies ↗

Appendix 4 · Reflection · Scope and value

Reflection

The prototype automates more than PowerPoint formatting: it calculates metric changes, summarises meeting material, groups findings and assembles an output. But it doesn’t automate much of the work surrounding that output.

Implemented automation and work that remains manual
Work involvedCoverage today
Find files and obtain missing updatesManual
Choose relevant / permitted evidenceManual
Prepare incompatible spreadsheetsManual · assisted intake not built
Calculate supported metric changesAutomated
Read, group and synthesise notesAI-assisted · errors / omissions possible
Format the report / presentationAutomated
Check accuracy, confidentiality and relevanceManual
Make decisions and follow upManual

More files ≠ more savings

More reading handled.
More checking required.

Contradictions, irrelevant material and longer outputs can increase correction and review effort.

1 spreadsheet · 12 documents40,000 characters of combined meeting text

Excess input is rejected. There is no tested large-document processing strategy.

Exact quotation checks cannot detect every omission or unsupported interpretation.

Scenario: 8h → 2h = 6h released

Six hours could be plausible if someone currently spends most of an eight-hour preparation process reading, calculating, copying and formatting. If most of those hours involve chasing people, understanding disagreements or deciding what to recommend, this prototype addresses a much smaller share.
